findings.consequence: A caller failure code 37 became success 0 in both shells; cleanup can also propagate a taskkill race exit.
findings.remediation: Preserve the prior global value or its absence in finally; retain process-tree termination checks.
findings.testGap: The original process test checked descendant termination but not native state.
findings.trigger: Windows cleanup executes taskkill after a caller native command.

findings.consequence: Shared persisted values receive different hashes even though their content is identical.
findings.remediation: Decode real apostrophe escapes without changing escaped literals or ordinary PS7 fingerprints.
findings.testGap: Portable tests covered dates and lint but not cross-serializer fingerprints.
findings.trigger: The same apostrophe-bearing JSON value is fingerprinted by PS5 and PS7.

findings.consequence: IO.EnumerationOptions is unavailable and inventory creation throws before discovering source files.
findings.remediation: Retain the modern path and add a compatible per-directory fallback with exclusions, link safety and explicit I/O failure behavior.
findings.testGap: Modern equivalence tests did not execute the helper successfully on legacy .NET Framework.
findings.trigger: A standalone source inventory helper runs under Windows PowerShell 5.1.

findings.consequence: The original escape-casing normalization produced identical hashes for distinct literal values, weakening change detection.
findings.remediation: Normalize escape casing only when backslash parity denotes an actual JSON Unicode escape.
findings.testGap: No test distinguished escaped Unicode characters from literal backslash-u text.
findings.trigger: Literal strings backslash-u-ABCD and backslash-u-abcd are fingerprinted.

findings.consequence: Retain=5 kept 5 result files but 12 metadata files after 12 writes. Per-argument metadata has no bound and increases directory/storage cost.
findings.remediation: Bound optional diagnostic metadata and benchmark one-pass result/metadata retention without changing cache correctness.
findings.testGap: Query-cache tests do not count retained metadata or stress distinct argument keys.
findings.trigger: A namespace receives many distinct query argument fingerprints.

findings.consequence: Retention throws IOException after the new result is successfully published, turning optional cleanup into a query failure.
findings.remediation: Allow atomic cache reads with delete sharing and make retention tolerate transient sharing conflicts; retain explicit publication failures.
findings.testGap: No leased-reader publication/retention scenario exists in the cache regression.
findings.trigger: A concurrent reader holds an old result with FileShare.Read while a new query triggers retention.
A button moves outside an @if block while added/removed normalized lines contain the same multiset.
findings.consequence: The old sorted comparison classified the behavioral change as presentation-only and skipped frontend contract regeneration.
findings.testGap: Only simple class edits and text changes were covered.
findings.remediation: Preserve normalized line sequence; add the conditional-scope regression and single-backslash bookkeeping normalization.

findings.trigger: Git core.quotepath quotes a tracked or untracked Unicode filename and its content changes with unchanged size/time.
findings.consequence: Text path parsing hashes a missing escaped path instead of the actual file; a previously passed verification receipt can remain valid after source changes.
findings.testGap: Receipt tests did not force quoted Unicode path output or equal-time edits.
findings.remediation: Use NUL path discovery, include both rename endpoints, test tracked/untracked Unicode content, and restore fixture-overwritten receipt bytes.

findings.trigger: Generation writes a matching input/output cache receipt for an architecture index that contains dependency, untracked-project or cycle drift.
findings.consequence: The old Check plus Reuse path returned exit 0 before enforcing drift counters.
findings.testGap: Cache reuse was not exercised with an explicitly nonzero architectural summary.
findings.remediation: Enforce all three drift counters on a cache hit; test each nonzero counter plus clean reuse.

findings.trigger: A module represented by an extracted application project has declared business dependencies in module-dependencies.json.
findings.consequence: The generated page discarded the edges and reported none observed; current Admin, Ai, Billing and other pages were wrong.
findings.testGap: Module inventory tests checked project presence but not dependency-line equivalence for each extracted module.
findings.remediation: Read declared graph edges for extracted modules and verify every generated dependency line against that graph.

findings.trigger: Wiki output contains canonical Modules/Services/Tooling/Hosts/Platform/scripts paths or Windows separators.
findings.consequence: Modern module paths disappear from referenced/scope paths; text test paths are shortened to an inner tests segment.
findings.testGap: Parser tests exercised legacy roots and did not compare structured and text output for the current repository layout.
findings.remediation: Add current repository roots while retaining existing path normalization, sorting, timeout and trace filtering.

findings.trigger: A tracked file is renamed out of a requested scope, including a move into a watcher-ignored tree.
findings.consequence: The scoped projection can report no change and preserve its prior fingerprint, allowing stale context reuse for a removed source.
findings.testGap: Existing rename test intentionally retained destination only and no regression exercised the old scope or ignored destination.
findings.remediation: Retain both rename endpoints in porcelain parsing and watcher pending paths; retain destination-only copy behavior.

findings.trigger: A cache key expires through TryGet or metrics pruning, is reinserted, and the cache later exceeds retention.
findings.consequence: Stale FIFO bookkeeping evicts the newly reinserted value before an older live key; repeated expiry also retains disconnected queue entries.
findings.testGap: Tests bounded dictionary entries but never expired/reinserted keys before FIFO overflow.
findings.remediation: Keep dictionary and FIFO node removal atomic under one Lock, with one linked node per active key and no disconnected queue history.

findings.trigger: The same worktree with a tracked rename is fingerprinted by Node and MCP, including Unicode or case-only paths.
findings.consequence: Different fingerprints prevent exact projection reuse; OEM-decoded Git paths become nonexistent mojibake paths and no longer identify the changed source. Case-insensitive identity and case conversion also disagree across runtimes.
findings.testGap: Previous scope tests did not run the real Node CLI against the same repository snapshot.
findings.remediation: Retain both rename endpoints, decode Git as UTF-8, preserve case-sensitive Git identities and use the same ordinal hash order in Node and C#.

findings.trigger: A current extracted module is selected by diff context after all application modules have moved to owning projects.
findings.consequence: Declared dependencies and downstream consumers become empty and module-owned test navigation disappears. Admin lost eight declared dependencies despite 46 current C# test files.
findings.testGap: Existing SQLite diff cases checked symbols and source hashes but not module graph edges or current focused test roots.
findings.remediation: Load declared graph entries for extracted modules and enumerate all current owned test roots through the existing module-root helper and NUL-safe Git inventory.

findings.trigger: A whole-pipeline receipt matches unchanged inputs and generated architecture output that contains drift after update.
findings.consequence: Check exits successfully before the architecture generator runs; its own cache gate cannot protect this shortcut.
findings.testGap: Previous cache fixture exercised only the architecture generator, not a valid whole-pipeline receipt.
findings.remediation: Before the whole-pipeline Check shortcut succeeds, enforce the same three required architecture summary counters. Retain fast receipt reuse for clean results.

findings.trigger: An unregistered requested group or a catalog group without an execution handler reaches affected smoke.
findings.consequence: Unknown execute returned success in 0 seconds and published a success receipt without running tests. Case variants can duplicate canonical group identity.
findings.testGap: Existing scheduler tests covered known catalog groups, but not rejected requested IDs or missing dispatch handlers.
findings.remediation: Validate unique requested/catalog identities, canonicalize aliases and throw from the default dispatch handler.

findings.trigger: A rejected mutating read-only command discards its contaminated snapshot while another reader waits for the same slot.
findings.consequence: The slot lease was released before removal, allowing a new reader to race with deletion of the checkout it acquired.
findings.testGap: Previous corruption recovery and stable-lock tests did not probe exclusivity at the contaminated removal boundaries.
findings.remediation: Remove contaminated ready marker and checkout while holding the lease, then release it in finally even when cleanup throws.

findings.trigger: A tracked or untracked Unicode file is already dirty, then content changes with equal size and preserved timestamp.
findings.consequence: Quoted line-based Git paths were hashed as missing files, leaving the verify-fast fingerprint unchanged and reusing stale success. Trim also changes legitimate leading-space identities.
findings.testGap: The cache tests only edited ASCII paths.
findings.remediation: Use the existing NUL-safe Git path inventory, disable rename collapsing for changed paths and preserve exact whitespace in path normalization.

findings.trigger: Ordinary scoped verification calls the publication writer without CompletedFullVerification.
findings.consequence: It hashes the full repository and every generated index before reporting that the full status is unchanged; it also fails on irrelevant missing full-gate inputs.
findings.testGap: Tests distinguished publication states but did not prove the scoped no-op avoids full-gate I/O.
findings.remediation: Return immediately for the explicitly scoped no-op, before manifest/source/index reads; retain Generation, Status and completed full Verification behavior.

findings.trigger: A scheduler writer terminates while its lock file remains, or a long-lived lock reaches age-based reclamation.
findings.consequence: Fresh ownerless files reject mutations for five to ten minutes; age is not live ownership. Stable-file deletion also risks changing the coordination identity on platforms that permit unlinking a held file.
findings.testGap: Registry/lifecycle checks did not terminate an actual lock holder or exercise fresh orphan and old live leases.
findings.remediation: All seven scheduler managers use persistent OpenOrCreate exclusive OS leases, dispose only the handle and retain the coordination file. Add real manager/child lease tests to the bounded catalog and bind their source inputs to group receipts.

findings.trigger: Referenced check IDs change in change-policies.json while workspace-policies.json and validator text remain unchanged.
findings.consequence: The validated JSON cache continues accepting a policy rejected by full validation; the workspace-policy stage also reuses its passed receipt because the dependency was absent from its fingerprint.
findings.testGap: Policy cache tests changed only its primary policy/validator and the fixture omitted referenced definitions.
findings.remediation: Bind dependency text and presence to the immutable cache entry, parse that captured input on a miss, and include the same dependency in workspace-policy stage fingerprints. Test equal-size/time edits, mode parity, missing-to-created, empty/malformed content and restoration.

findings.trigger: A facade/runner invokes prune on a fresh scheduler under StrictMode.
findings.consequence: Schedule plan, orchestration cycle and watchdog response construction reads BaseName directly from an empty collection and throws instead of returning a valid empty result.
findings.testGap: Standalone new lease tests initially inherited permissive mode; the real bounded gate exposed the strict caller context.
findings.remediation: Enumerate candidate names through the pipeline and explicitly enable StrictMode in the real seven-manager lease fixture. Preserve the full legacy lease test with a fresh orphan/stable-file assertion matching the new lifecycle contract.
